correctness.rationale: For each possible uniform parent V, a new terminal appears and V loses terminal status iff V was terminal. Sibling pairs gain ℓ_V when V is nonterminal and lose ℓ_parent(V)-1 otherwise. The sum of those losses over all terminal V is 2C. Crucially E(ΔL ΔC|tree)=L/n. These give exact recurrences for E L, E L², E C and E LC. Bases at n=2 and n=3 and induction yield Cov(L,C)=\(n/8\) for n≥4 and slope \(3/2\). An independent birth-index product yields Pr(i,j terminal siblings)=(i-1)/((n-1)(n-2)). Exact enumerations through n=8 and moment recurrences through n=150 passed 6596 rational assertions; unbounded validity rests on the algebraic proof, not enumeration.

originality.rationale: The inspected 2008 primary paper handles leaf counts in uniform recursive trees but cherries in a different Yule splitting process. Janson’s outdegree-count covariance formulas concern degree classes rather than leaf-child adjacency, which is not determined by the degree-class counts. The later 2025 leaf-neighbor-profile analysis and published mathematical research records provide no directly covering exact joint moment. The surviving novelty is the \(n/8\) finite-size covariance and universal \(3/2\) linear slope, not the classical \(n/2\) leaf mean; an inaccessible older full text and implicit motif moment expansions remain specific residual risks.

value.rationale: Global terminal count and local sibling clustering are basic and noninterchangeable random-tree summary statistics: the degree-class count of terminals does not say whether two terminals share a parent. A closed positive covariance \(n/8\) for every tree order and a sample-size invariant least-squares slope \(3/2\) quantify this relationship exactly; the birth-order-resolved pair law gives independent structural explanation and a second route to the mean. This is a natural mixed-moment question motivated by classical recursive-tree leaf laws and the distinction from Yule sibling counts; neither exact correctness nor the mere novelty search is the value argument.
